mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by > 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by RSAFS) indicates weakening consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate revenues and thus leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where RSAFS shows a sustained 3-month decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increases by > 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within a quarter signals a strong supply-side expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where INDPRO increases by > 2% within a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) both decline by more than 5% within a quarter, it signals a broad-based weakening of demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 5% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline by > 5% within a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) declines by more than 100,000 in a month, it signals a significant labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% and PAYEMS declines > 100,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 5% and PAYEMS declines by > 100,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% signals inflationary pressure, which erodes real returns and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL increases by > 2% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters, it signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative growth for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 shows negative growth for two consecutive quarters.
